research_question: Can a cross-channel analysis distinguish pointlike Standard-Model fermions from finite-size, contact-interaction, or excited-state alternatives under explicit EFT and systematic-uncertainty controls?

subhypotheses.claim: A common resolution ledger can connect high-energy and lepton-hadron observables without treating their systematics as identical.
A contact-interaction deviation requires explicit EFT validity and flavor assumptions before it can be interpreted as compositeness evidence.
Excited-state and form-factor hypotheses require separate likelihood shapes and cannot be collapsed into one generic new-physics term.
The SM field inventory is a current, testable description rather than a proof against every higher-scale degree of freedom.

claim_constraints: Do not state that quarks or leptons are proven indivisible at all scales.
Do not describe protons or neutrons as elementary particles.
Do not say that all bosons are force carriers.
Do not convert future-facility projections into observed results.
Do not identify an EFT contact coefficient with a unique microscopic constituent model.
